re-correlophus-ciliatus.title: Crested Gecko
re-correlophus-ciliatus.summary: A tree-climbing gecko from New Caledonia that eats mostly a prepared fruit-based diet. ReptiFiles rates it low difficulty.
rows: About 8 in snout to tail. Adults weigh 35–45 g
Tall, climbing setup: 18 × 18 × 36 in (L × W × H) minimum for one adult
Top (warm) 82–85°F, bottom 70–75°F, night 65–72°F. Avoid long stretches above 85°F
60–80%. Mist daily, and let it dry to about 50% between mistings to prevent mold
Low-level UVB is recommended (UVI 1–2 at the top branch). Day/night cycle, no night lights
Complete powdered crested gecko diet mixed with water. Juveniles get it daily plus insects 1–2× a week. Adults get it every 2–3 days plus insects 0–1× a week. Fruit only as an occasional treat
Build up slowly. Start with 5-minute sessions every other day, then go up to about 15 minutes once it stays calm (no more than about 20 minutes a day). They jump, so handle over a soft surface
Most active at dusk and dawn. Climbs and leaps
notes: A dropped tail does not grow back.
Don't house males together. Two females need at least twice the minimum space.
